properties.name: TransDigm Group Incorporated
properties.fact: This company designs high-end aerospace components for commercial planes and the U.S. Military.

properties.name: Celanese Corporation
properties.fact: Celanese Acetate products are made from cellulose - a renewable, sustainable resource sourced from managed forests. Acetate yarns were initially developed as an alternative to silk.

properties.name: Royal Gold, Inc.
properties.fact: Royal Gold is one of the world's leading precious metal streams, but the company did not start there. In fact, the firm started as an oil-exploration company.

properties.name: Simpson Manufacturing Co., Inc.
properties.fact: With seven accredited state-of-the-art test labs, Simpson has supported 98% of the top 100 builders.

properties.name: New Fortress Energy Inc.
properties.fact: Wes Edens was dedicated to reducing carbon emissions and fostering economic development through universal access to cleaner, affordable, and reliable energy. So, Wes decided to do something about it in 2014 when he founded New Fortress. The work of his company has improved the lives of millions through its liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals, power generation facilities, and logistics assets across the world.

properties.name: Albemarle Corporation
properties.fact: In late November of 2020, the world's top lithium producer Albemarle joined forces with 27 companies, including electric vehicles maker Tesla and ride share company Uber, to form a group that is pushing for 100% electric vehicle sales in the US by 2030.

properties.name: Diamondback Energy, Inc.
properties.fact: Diamondback Energy uses horizontal drilling to reduce surface use and impact. It also increases production rate by increasing the ratio of wellbore length exposed to the "pay zone".

properties.name: Alaska Air Group, Inc.
properties.fact: Contrary to popular belief, Alaska Airlines is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

properties.name: Matson, Inc.
properties.fact: Alexander & Baldwin began as one of Hawaii's original "Big Five" sugarcane corporations. Some of the company founders were 19th century medical missionaries. Today, A&B is one of Hawaii's largest commercial real estate firms.

properties.name: DuPont de Nemours, Inc.
properties.fact: In 1929, Dow hires its first female researcher, Sylvia Stoesser. Five of her patents helped unlock the secrets to treating oil wells.

properties.name: General Dynamics Corporation
properties.fact: General Dynamics constructs the M1 Abrams Tank, the main battle tank for the United States of America military.

properties.name: Trex Company, Inc.
properties.fact: Trex Company is the world's largest manufacturer of wood-alternative decking and railing. The company's composite products are made of 95% recycled materials and it redirects roughly 400 million pounds of plastic and scrap wood from landfills every year.

properties.name: Philip Morris International Inc.
properties.fact: Although the Marlboro Man is one of the most widely recognized advertising images in history, a little known fact is that the Marlboro brand was originally marketed in the 1920sas a cigarette for women using the ad slogan "Mild as May."

properties.name: Koppers Holdings Inc.
properties.fact: Founded in 1912. by a German immigrant named Heinrich Koppers, this company is one of the largest providers of railroad crossties. Koppers  three divisions are: Railroad and Utility Products & Services, Performance Chemicals, and Carbon Materials and Chemicals.

properties.name: Valero Energy Corporation
properties.fact: Named for the mission San Antonio de Valero  the original name of the Alamo  Valero Energy Corporation was created on Jan. 1, 1980, as the corporate successor of LoVaca Gathering Company, a subsidiary of the Coastal States Gas Corporation.

properties.name: Slb N.V.
properties.fact: In 2018, they invested close to $700 million in research for oilfield activities.

properties.name: EQT Corporation
properties.fact: EQT is the largest producer of natural gas in the United States of America.

properties.name: Antero Midstream Corporation
properties.fact: Antero Resources completed the largest independent E&P IPO to date, reaching $1.8 billion in proceeds.

properties.name: GE Aerospace
properties.fact: In 1896, GE became one of the original 12 companies listed on the Dow Jones industrial average. It was founded by Thomas Edison and J.P. Morgan.

properties.name: Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc.
properties.fact: The water company has more than 20 billion feet of pipe in service around the world and it is the largest maker of high-density polyethylene pipe in the United States of America.

properties.name: Aemetis, Inc.
properties.fact: Aemetis means "One Prudent Wisdom", referring to the prudence and wisdom of replacing petroleum with renewable fuels and chemicals.

properties.name: Stifel Financial Corp
properties.fact: The predecessor of Stifel Financial was founded in 1890 and became the first North American firm, outside of New York, to provide underwriting activities on behalf of a South American country.

properties.name: Carlisle Companies Incorporated
properties.fact: Carlisle Companies started with very humble beginnings by manufacturing bicycle inner tubes. Now, the company has a very diversified portfolio of services and products doing over $4.2 billion in revenue in 2020.

properties.name: Occidental Petroleum Corporation
properties.fact: In 2018, this company was the 9th largest producer of petroleum in Texas.

properties.name: LyondellBasell Industries N.V.
properties.fact: Their chemicals are used to make coatings for wind turbines that reduce drag and extend blade life

properties.name: Exxon Mobil Corporation
properties.fact: The Wright Brothers used fuel and lubricant from Exxon in their first flight.

properties.name: Northrop Grumman Corporation
properties.fact: Based in the state of Virginia, Northrop Grumman produces drones, warplanes, aircraft components, and radar systems.

properties.name: The Mosaic Company
properties.fact: Mosaic is the largest producer of finished phosphate products with an annual capacity greater than the next two largest producers combined.

properties.name: RPM International Inc.
properties.fact: In 1947, the original product that the company sold was a heavy-duty aluminum roof coating, which is still sold to this day. In that first year, the business reported $90,000 in sales.

properties.name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.
properties.fact: In 1925, the Huff Daland Dusters, a predecessor of Delta, is founded. Huff Daland was the first commercial agriculture flying company. At the time, Huff Daland's 18 planes became the largest privately-owned fleet in the world.

properties.name: Antero Resources Corporation
properties.fact: Antero holds over 612,000 net acres in two of the lowest-cost natural gas and natural gas liquids basins in North America: the Marcellus Shale and Utica Shale

properties.name: Houlihan Lokey, Inc.
properties.fact: The company has executed more than 1,500 restructuring transactions, totaling over $3 trillion. That amount is larger than the GDP of the United Kingdom.

properties.name: Tyson Foods, Inc.
properties.fact: Tyson produces 1 in 5 pounds of all chicken, beef, and pork in the U.S.

properties.name: National Fuel Gas Company
properties.fact: National Fuel Gas Company was one of the earliest gas utility companies in the U.S., which means that it witnessed several technological firsts. One of the firsts in the industry was the development of a gas-fired generator to produce electricity for cathodic protection, which fought against corrosion on pipelines.

properties.name: Cabot Corp.
properties.fact: Do you use an inkjet printer? Cabot helped pioneer aqueous inkjet colorants. The company is a specialty chemicals and materials company.

properties.name: Freeport-McMoRan Inc.
properties.fact: One of the founders of Freeport-McMoRan, Eric Pierson Swenson, was among the first Swedes to settle in Texas. His father, Swante Swensen, bought Texas Railroad Certificates to acquire land and was inducted into the Hall of Great Westerners at the National Cowboy and Westerner Museum.

properties.name: HEICO Corporation
properties.fact: Since 1990, Heico has acquired over eighty specialized businesses.

properties.name: BWX Technologies, Inc.
properties.fact: BWX has spent 60+ years in nuclear innovation, with over 400 reactors delivered for Naval Nuclear Power and more than 314 steam generators delivered to nuclear power plants.

properties.name: Targa Resources Corp.
properties.fact: Targa Resources is a Fortune 500 company with just under 3,000 employees.

properties.name: Altria Group, Inc.
properties.fact: In 1978, Altria, then Philip Morris, purchased the Seven-Up Company.

properties.name: Eagle Materials Inc.
properties.fact: Eagle Materials is an American company and makes that clear to everyone - all of its manufactured products are 100% made in the USA.

properties.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company
properties.fact: In 1986, ADM formed the Golden Peanut Company.

properties.name: The Sherwin-Williams Company
properties.fact: In 1940 Canadian Norman Breakey invented the first paint roller. He didn't profit from it because he never patented it. During World War II, an inventor working for Sherwin-Williams also created a roller brush because the hogs hair used for paintbrushes was unavailable due to the war.

properties.name: Curtiss-Wright Corporation
properties.fact: Curtis-Wright claims to have the most renowned legacy in the aerospace industry after having been formed by the titans of aviation Glenn Curtis, the father of naval aviation, and the Wright brothers, who were credited with the first flight of mankind. When the company consolidated in 1929, it immediately became the country's largest aviation company, which positioned it nicely to build over 142,000 aircraft for the U.S. military during WWII.

properties.name: NovaGold Resources Inc.
properties.fact: NovaGold is a pure gold play focused on Alaska's Donlin Gold prospect - one of the world's largest gold mines, with 39 million ounces of estimated mineral resource.

properties.name: UFP Industries, Inc.
properties.fact: UFP shipped its first load of treated lumber to The Home Depot in 1979, which was a brand new company at the time.

properties.name: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
properties.fact: In the mid-1950's Air Products gained an opportunity from the launching of the first Sputnik, which American scientists surmised was powered by liquid hydrogen. The U.S. also wanted liquid hydrogen, and Air Products was asked to supply it. As a security precaution, the new Air Products Company plants were provided with code names like "Baby-Bear" and "Project Rover". One large plant was disguised as the "Apix Fertilizer Company".

properties.name: Range Resources Corporation
properties.fact: As of the end of 2021, Range Resources had 17.775 trillion cubic feet of natural gas equivalent of estimated proved reserves. Most of the land they own is in the Marcellus Shale.

properties.name: PPG Industries, Inc.
properties.fact: PPG has a long history of innovation. Started in 1883, the company was instrumental in breaking European monopoly on the production of plate glass. Within 40 years, PPG had become the largest glass producer in the nation. In the 1950's, the company developed the first latex-based interior paints. Today, the company researches, develops, and manufactures some of the most advanced coatings on the planet.

properties.name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
properties.fact: CF manufactures dozens of nitrogen products for agricultural and industrial uses.

properties.name: Matador Resources Company
properties.fact: Joseph Foran and Scott King founded Matador Resources Company with an initial $6 million investment to show how confident they were in their future endeavor. This sparked an additional $46.8 million from various investors, which enabled the company to expand to what it is now.

properties.name: Corteva, Inc.
properties.fact: Former U.S. vice president Henry Wallace founded Hi-Bred Corn Company, one of Corteva's predecessor company's.

properties.name: Commercial Metals Company
properties.fact: Commercial Metals Company's rebar can be found in many structures - including the AT&T Stadium in Dallas, the Pentagon, essential highways and bridges, and other modern landmarks all over the world.

properties.name: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co.
properties.fact: The steel company was founded in 1939 by Thomas Neilan and largely produced rebar. Now the company distributes approximately 100,000 different metal products.

properties.name: Allegiant Travel Company
properties.fact: Allegiant Travel is an ultra low-cost U.S. airline and one of the 15 largest in North America.

properties.name: Teekay Tankers Ltd.
properties.fact: Teekay claims to be the world's largest operator of mid-sized tankers. Its "SuezMax" tankers are classified as such because they are the largest size ship that will still fit through the Suez Canal.

properties.name: APA Corporation
properties.fact: Apache Oil Corporation was founded on December 6, 1954, in Minneapolis by Truman Anderson, Raymond Plank, and Charles Arnao. The company started with six employees and $250,000 in funding. The company's name started with the founders' initials A, P, and A. Che was added to the end at the suggestion of Helen Johnson, an early employee who was awarded a $25 U.S. savings bond for the idea.

properties.name: Owens Corning
properties.fact: The Pink Panther regularly appears as the company's mascot, showing up in most of the advertisement for the world's largest manufacturer of fiberglass composites.

properties.name: Century Aluminum Company
properties.fact: With operations in the U.S., Iceland, and Netherlands, Century Aluminum manufactures high quality, high purity aluminum and carbon anodes.

properties.name: California Resources Corp
properties.fact: CRC is committed to energy transition in the sector and has some of the lowest carbon intensity production in the U.S.

properties.name: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd.
properties.fact: The American company traces its origins to a German firm, which began in 1866 painting carriages. As the automotive industry progressed, the company pivoted toward coating automotive vehicles. The firm now operates in over 120 counties and has more than 100,000 customers.

properties.name: Bank of America Corporation
properties.fact: By the 1920s, the Bank of Italy was the only statewide bank in California. Along with offices in New York and Italy, and with a vision to one day have financial centers across the country, the bank changed its name to Bank of America in 1930. By 1945, it became the largest bank in the world.

properties.name: Ovintiv Inc.
properties.fact: The company traces its roots back to the 1880s when the Canadian Pacific Railway received compensation for subsurface rights for a large portion of Alberta and Saskatchewan. Those rights would later be spun off to the company's predecessors. Years later, while drilling for water, the staff of Canadian Pacific Railway discovered natural gas.

properties.name: Southwest Airlines Co.
properties.fact: Southwest Airlines wasn't the airline's original name. It was called "Air Southwest" until 1971.

properties.name: Howmet Aerospace Inc.
properties.fact: Founded in 1888, by Charles Martin Hall (who discovered the process for smelting aluminum) and industrialist Alfred Hunt, Alcoa is one of the world's top 10 producers of aluminum. The company produces primary aluminum, fabricated aluminum, and combined aluminum. Operations include technology, mining, refining, smelting, fabricating, and recycling.

properties.name: Eastman Chemical Company
properties.fact: The Chemicals from Coal Facility of Eastman Chemical Company was the first in the United States of America to use coal rather than petroleum as a raw material in acetyl chemicals' commercial production.

properties.name: Phillips 66
properties.fact: Phillips has a global refining capacity of 2.2 million barrels of crude oil per day.

properties.name: Balchem Corp
properties.fact: A group of entrepreneurs, investors, and doctors started Balchem, which was initially housed in a laboratory on the top floor of the Chemists Club in New York City.

properties.name: Steel Dynamics, Inc.
properties.fact: As of 2021, the steel company is domestically ranked the third largest producer of carbon steel products.

properties.name: Nucor Corporation
properties.fact: In 1905, Ransom E. Olds, creator of the Oldsmobile, had a dispute with stockholders and left his own company  Olds Motor Works. He soon formed REO Motor Company, which evolved into the Nuclear Corporation of America and ultimately, Nucor.

properties.name: Linde plc
properties.fact: In October 2018, Praxair and Linde AG came together to create Linde plc, the UK's leading industrial gas and engineering company.

properties.name: Texas Pacific Land Corporation
properties.fact: The company was created through a federal charter for the construction of a transcontinental railroad from Texas to California. Ten years later in 1881, T&P had completed 972 miles of track across 3.5 million acres of land in Texas.

properties.name: Wells Fargo & Company
properties.fact: The company operates 12 museums, most known as a Wells Fargo History Museum. Displays include original stagecoaches, photographs, gold nuggets and mining artifacts, the Pony Express, telegraph equipment and historic bank artifacts.

properties.name: FMC Corporation
properties.fact: FMC's history includes production of firetruck pumps, as well as military equipment.

properties.name: Citigroup Inc.
properties.fact: During the war of 1812, the United States of America' currency and treasury bills were losing value, trade was languishing, and businesses were failing. In mid-July, City Bank of New York appointed a committee of directors to "make proper arrangements for removing the books, cash, etc., belonging to the bank, in case of the invasion of the city by the enemy."

properties.name: The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company
properties.fact: In 1868, a Civil War veteran, Orlando Scott, opened a hardware store where he sold weed-free seed to local farmers. Soon after he refined his product, he sold his product to homeowners, which was the first time anyone developed and sold seeds to the open market.

properties.name: SkyWest, Inc.
properties.fact: With 620+ aircraft, SkyWest is a regional airline. It also leases aircraft and spare engines. The company was founded in 1972.

properties.name: International Flavors & Fragrances Inc.
properties.fact: IFF had a goal to reduce GHG emissions intensity by 25%. They actually reduced it by 33.8%.

properties.name: The Williams Companies, Inc.
properties.fact: Williams traces its history to 1908, when brothers S. Miller Williams, Jr. and David R. Williams were working for a construction contractor who had an order to pave sidewalks in Fort Smith, Arkansas.

properties.name: H.B. Fuller Company
properties.fact: H.B. Fuller Company was founded in 1887, you guessed it, by Harvey Benjamin Fuller. The company's legacy began with the introduction of Fuller's Premium Liquid Fish Glue, which was considered to be able to "cement everything." Although it was the first, H.B. Fuller Company was not going to stop its innovative spirit with the Liquid Fish Glue, in fact, Fisher was just getting started.

properties.name: Baker Hughes Company
properties.fact: In January of 2019, Baker Hughes made an announcement that they plan to reduce Scope 1 and 2 operating emissions by 50% by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2050.

properties.name: DT Midstream, Inc.
properties.fact: DT is among the first midstream companies to implement a program set to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

properties.name: MP Materials Corp.
properties.fact: From 1965 to 1995, Mountain Pass produced the majority of global rare earth materials. So infamous, it was coined the "Mountain Pass Era."

properties.name: Warrior Met Coal, Inc.
properties.fact: One of Alabama's largest coal mine operators, Warrior Met supplies non-thermal metallurgical coal to help power blast furnances for the global steel industry. Clients range into Europe, South America, and Asia.

properties.name: Halliburton Company
properties.fact: Halliburton's fascinating and proud history reveals a continuous focus on innovation and expansion that began with the company's founder, Erle P. Halliburton. After borrowing a wagon, a team of mules and a pump, he built a wooden mixing box and started an oil well cementing business in Duncan, Oklahoma.

properties.name: Vulcan Materials Company
properties.fact: In 1957, Vulcan Materials Company asked stockholders to approve a merger involving nine companies at the same time Union Chemicals, Lambert Brothers, and seven other related corporations. Fortune Magazine observed that the prospectus issued for the transaction was one of the most complex ever printed.

properties.name: Devon Energy Corporation
properties.fact: In 1950, Devon co-founder John Nichols created the first public oil and gas drilling fund registered with the SEC.

properties.name: International Paper Company
properties.fact: More than 90 percent of International Papers fiber supply in the United States of America comes from privately owned forests, most of which are small and family-owned.

properties.name: United Airlines Holdings, Inc.
properties.fact: United Boeing 247s flew the same route on the Main Line that settlers followed to the West. The 247 could cross North America in a single night and was the first modern airline

properties.name: Textron Inc.
properties.fact: Textron's subsidiary, Bell Helicopter, was pivotal in the Vietnam war. The Army embraced Bell's AH-1 Cobra because of its slim profile and lightweight plexiglass canopy.

properties.name: Johnson Controls International plc
properties.fact: Warren Johnson toils for three years to invent a device to regulate room temperature. In 1883, he receives his first patent for what will be known as the electric room thermostat an invention that launches an industry and changes how people live.

properties.name: Element Solutions Inc
properties.fact: The roots of Element Solutions date back to a metal finishing company that was founded in 1785.

properties.name: Caesarstone Ltd.
properties.fact: In 1987, Caesarstone sparked a revolution in the global countertops market by developing the first quartz surfacing solution - enabling the rise of man-made quartz countertops as a viable alternative to granite.

properties.name: Armstrong World Industries, Inc.
properties.fact: AWI dates back 155 years to a two-man cork-cutting shop in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. When Thomas Armstrong started selling his product, he put his name on every bag of Armstrong corks with a written guarantee inside the bag because he believed in what he did. His pioneering and American spirit wanted to ensure that "the buyer have faith."

properties.name: Huntsman Corporation
properties.fact: Huntsman created a "clamshell" container for the McDonald's Big Mac, which is just one of 80 product inventions.

properties.name: Martin Marietta Materials, Inc.
properties.fact: in 2009, Fortune magazine ranked Martin Marietta Materials No. 1 on its "World's Most Admired Company for Building Materials Industry" list.

properties.name: SM Energy Company
properties.fact: From its founding in 1908, the SM Energy Company was known as St. Mary Land and Exploration Company until 2010.

properties.name: Ecolab Inc.
properties.fact: Ecolab's roots can be traced back to the 1920s, where M.J. Osborn recognized the need for an effective detergent for electric dish machines.

properties.name: Woodward, Inc.
properties.fact: Woodward is very proud of the parts they supplied for the United States of America military's first turbine-powered aircraft.

properties.name: EOG Resources, Inc.
properties.fact: In 2015, EOG produced a cumulative 285 million barrels of oil from the Eagle Ford Shale.

properties.name: Sensient Technologies Corporation
properties.fact: Founded in 1882, Sensient was originally a distillery, but due to the prohibition, the company then transformed into the food industry. In 2021, Sensient Technologies was ranked 10th on the Global Top 50 Food Flavors and Fragrances Companies list.

properties.name: Teekay Corporation
properties.fact: Teekay claims to be the world's largest operator of mid-sized tankers. Its "SuezMax" tankers are classified as such because they are the largest size ship that will still fit through the Suez Canal.

properties.name: Olin Corporation
properties.fact: During both WWI and WWII, Olin played a key role in producing ammunitions and guns. Supporting the war efforts made the Olin's family one of the wealthiest American families of that time.

properties.name: Cheniere Energy, Inc.
properties.fact: Cheniere specializes in liquified natural gas (LNG) and was the first U.S. company to export LNG. The company has a 25 year agreement to provide LNG to Taiwan, valued at $25 billion through the year 2046

properties.name: RTX Corporation
properties.fact: Raytheon is a large military contractor, earning much of its revenue from the United States of America government. Products engineered include military defense systems, aviation technology, and  even intelligent space technology.

properties.name: Hexcel Corporation
properties.fact: Founded in the basement of Roger Steel's suburban home after Steel and co-founder Roscoe Hughes returned home from the Navy post-WWII. Their innovations and hard work would not stop in that basement. In fact,  Hexcel went on to produce the lunar struts of the Apollo 11 lunar landing module.

properties.name: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc.
properties.fact: Sharing a name with protagonist of the video game series, "God of War", Kratos leadership has deep experience working with the U.S. Dept of Defense, Dept of Homeland Security, and various branches of the military. The company is involved in drone, missile defense, electronic warfare, space systems, communications, and training systems.

properties.name: Murphy Oil Corporation
properties.fact: In 1953, Charlie Murphy Sr. backed the development of a submersible drilling barge that took offshore rigs into deep waters. This development was fundamental for deepwater offshore drilling - so they named the prototype the "Mr. Charlie."

properties.name: Delek US Holdings, Inc.
properties.fact: Having nothing to do with "Dr. Who", Delek refines over 300,000 barrels of crude oil each day at its four refineries.

properties.name: Vital Farms, Inc.
properties.fact: Enjoy eggs? Vital Farms is obsessed with them. Every Vital Farms organic egg comes for a pasture-raised hen.

properties.name: Builders FirstSource, Inc.
properties.fact: In 2020, the Fortune 500 company had just shy of $20 billion in sales with over 25,000 employees and over 500 locations.

properties.name: Newmont Corporation
properties.fact: Newmont is currently the world's largest corporate producer of gold, with over 5.8 million ounces mined in calendar year 2020. With operations in North America, South America, Africa, and Australia, the company also produces copper, silver, zinc, and lead. Canada-based Barrick Gold is a top competitor.

properties.name: American Airlines Group Inc.
properties.fact: In 1973, American Airlines hired the first female pilot for a commercial airline. Her name is Bonnie Tiburzi who, at 24 years old, started her job with American. She stayed with the company for 26 years. She was the first woman in the world to earn a Flight Engineer rating on a turbo-jet aircraft.

properties.name: ONEOK, Inc.
properties.fact: ONEOKs operations include a 38,000-mile integrated network of NGL and natural gas pipelines, processing plants, fractionators and storage facilities in the Mid-Continent, Williston, Permian and Rocky Mountain regions.

properties.name: L3Harris Technologies, Inc.
properties.fact: L3Harris has provided navigation technology for every U.S. GPS satellite ever launched. Nearly 3.3 million U.S. jobs rely heavily on GPS tech.

properties.name: Ashland Inc.
properties.fact: Ashland was founded in 1924, by three Swiss Oil executives, with an initial capital investment of $250,000.

properties.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
properties.fact: The commercial airplane Lockheed Martin is working on is intended to be the world's first supersonic business jet, flying at three times the speed of sound. At that speed, a plane could cross the country in about 90 minutes, four times faster than the current 5-6 hour flight time.

properties.name: Masco Corporation
properties.fact: The company's first contract came in 1930 with the Hudson Motor Company valued at $7,000.00

properties.name: Copa Holdings, S.A.
properties.fact: Copa Holdings is Panama's leader in airline passenger and cargo services.

properties.name: Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc.
properties.fact: Virgin Galactic blasted its founder, Sir Richard Branson, into space on July 11, 2021. Though he once declined being dropped 354 ft over Africa's Victoria Falls in a specially designed container, Branson had no qualms about being launched 53.5 miles above the earth's crust to become both the first billionaire and knight to reach the requisite altitude. His rival, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, would follow just nine days later in a spacecraft developed by his own company, Blue Origin.

properties.name: Quaker Houghton
properties.fact: With over 4k employees serving more than 110 countries, Quaker claims to be the global leader in industrial process fluids.

properties.name: JetBlue Airways Corporation
properties.fact: The founders of this New York-based company initially wanted to call the airline "Taxi" and to have a yellow livery to associate with New York. However, that idea was shot down by investors, so the founders settled on "NewAir," which was later changed to Jet Blue Airways.

properties.name: Rayonier Advanced Materials Inc.
properties.fact: Rayonier Advanced Materials is a pioneer in manufacturing the highest quality wood-based acetate-grade cellulose - so high-quality, in fact, that it is used in creation of LCD touch screens. In addition, the company manufactures high-value ethers used to develop slow-release medications, specialty cellulose for advanced automotive filters, hot dog and sausage casings, and even fluff pulp used in super absorbent diapers.

properties.name: Frontline Plc
properties.fact: Frontline operates a global fleet of some of the world's largest ships, including Suezmax, Aframax, and VLCC vessels. Several exceed 300,000 metric tons.

properties.name: Louisiana-Pacific Corporation
properties.fact: As of 2022, LP is the largest producer of oriented strand board (OSB) in the world.

properties.name: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc.
properties.fact: Cleveland-Cliffs earliest predecessor, The Cleveland Iron Mining Company, has its roots dating back to its founding in 1847. The company discovered rich iron-ore deposits in the highlands of Michigan and shortly after the first Soo Locks were opened and iron ore was transported between the Great Lakes and distributed throughout America. In 2022, the Cleveland-Cliffs is considered the largest flat-rolled steel producer in North America.

properties.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
properties.fact: The company operates the nations largest refining system with more than 3 million barrels per day of crude oil capacity across 16 refineries.

properties.name: Kinder Morgan, Inc.
properties.fact: Kinder Morgan operates enough pipelines to circle the Earth more than three times. Out of its 84,000 miles of pipeline, 70,000 miles carry 38% of the gas consumed in the U.S.

properties.name: Avient Corporation
properties.fact: Avient is a component of the S&P 400. Its products are diversified across several industries, including thermoplastics, plastic colorants and additives, thermoplastic resins, and vinyl resins.

properties.name: U.S. Bancorp
properties.fact: Fortune named U.S. Bank of the the 2020 World's Most Admired Companies. They were also ranked top ten in multiple other categories including social responsibility, use of corporate assets, financial soundness, long-term investment value, and management quality.

properties.name: Royal Bank of Canada
properties.fact: The largest bank in Canada, Royal Bank of Canada has over 16 million customers and well over $1 trillion in assets. Founded in 1864, it is has recently been ranked as one of the ten largest banks in the world.

properties.name: Asian Paints Limited
properties.fact: Asian Paints follows the 70:20:10 rule of learning - meaning 70% is learnt on the job, 20% through observation, and 10% in classrooms. Started in a garage, but now one of India's largest companies, AP's mascot for several decades was "Gattu" - a mischievous boy with a paint bucket in hand.

properties.name: ING Groep N.V.
properties.fact: ING operates in more than 40 countries. It is traditionally the market leader in the Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg.

properties.name: Champion Iron Limited
properties.fact: Though based in Australia, Champion Iron owns and operates Canada's Bloom Lake Mining Complex, located in Quebec.

properties.name: PI Industries Limited
properties.fact: PI Industries  manufactures agricultural and fine chemicals, crop protection products, nutrients, and polymers. The company has filed over 100 patent applications and recently entered pharmaceuticals, in 2020.

properties.name: The Sandur Manganese & Iron Ores Limited
Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V.
Washington H. Soul Pattinson and Company Limited
Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais S.A.
Coal India Limited
properties.fact: Owned by the Indian government, Coal India Ltd is the largest producer of coal in the world. The company produced almost 600 million tons of goal in 2021 alone.

properties.name: SigmaRoc plc
properties.fact: Sigmaroc invests in high quality quarries throughout Northern Europe, Scandanavia, and the UK. 76 sites produce approximately 1.3 billion tons of materials.

properties.name: The Boeing Company
properties.fact: Typically, about 50 gallons (189 liters) of paint are used to paint the typical 737. Once the paint is dry, it will weigh approximately 250 pounds (113 kilograms) per airplane, depending on the paint scheme.

properties.name: ArcelorMittal S.A.
